data.desc: One command lists the UI graph's handlers no recorded check exercised; a kept `actions` step replays under test

body:
**Version:** escher-0.3.0 · Epoch 3 — The UI graph (its last entry) · capabilities v030-07 (claimed by this chunk) and
v030-06 (named beside it: its owed test is this chunk's).

Handler coverage — one command: the handlers no recorded check exercised, read from the UI graph (v030-07)  CARRY: a
kept `actions` step's replay is owed a test, not accepted by construction — `Check::replay` runs every instance-verb
step through `Session::run`, so it holds by construction, unmeasured; this entry writes the test, and v030-06 reads
verified only once it passes (the operator's direction at the 2026-11-08 wrap, relaying the overseer and the founder:
escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here/inputs/I6-relay-1.md.txt; record: 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here's
report, Outcome and Addendum 1)

- intent §Findings 6 (E3), `escher-0.3.0/intent` `fct-3691127e9f`: «Nothing says which handlers no check reached» →
  «One command lists the handlers no recorded check exercised. Both read the D2 graph.»
- v030-07 requirement: «One command lists the handlers no recorded check exercised, read from the UI graph».

- v030-07 acceptance as the ledger holds it (`planned`, unclaimed): «After a set of recorded checks has run on the stand,
  one command lists exactly the handlers none of them exercised.» Method `integration`.

1. **The handler-coverage command.** One command that, after a set of recorded checks (kept checks, `check-{n}.json`,
   `Check::from_bytes` → `Check::replay`) has run on the stand, lists exactly the UI graph's handlers — a graph node's id
   and a handler's event name, as `DioxusDocument::graph` reads them (`GraphNode.handlers`, `GraphHandler.event`) — that
   none of those checks exercised.

2. **The canvas limit, stated in the acceptance** (the founder's checklist row and the overseer's reconnaissance item 4,
   cited below once snapped): the command counts the handlers the UI graph reads — DOM listeners on agent-visible nodes,
   one per (node, event) — so handlers a canvas dispatches internally, inside one listener, are not counted; 0.4.0
   extends the count to virtual nodes rather than redefining it. The command's shape keeps that extension open (keyed on
   the graph's node id with its optional `owner`, never on a `NodeId`). This adds no 0.4.0 capability.

3. **The owed replay test (CARRY `cry-sxrivdk3`, folded).** A test that records a session holding an `actions` step,
   keeps it as a check, reads it back through `Check::from_bytes` and replays it through `Check::replay` on a fresh
   session of the same app, the replay holding (the `actions` step accepted as kept and its answer equal to the kept
   one) — and a replay whose `actions` answer differs names the step and the differing key. v030-06 reads `verified`
   only once that test passes (the operator's direction, 2026-11-08 wrap, and again at this take-up — relay below);
   its ledger state today is `implemented`, unclaimed, ref kept, so it lies outside the `planned, unclaimed` pool and
   is named here explicitly.

- Read-only over the screen: the coverage read changes nothing, runs no step of its own, and carries no control value,
  typed text, page text beyond what the `graph` verb already carries (ids, component and event names), or `NodeId`.

- No canvas renderer, no virtual-node production, no `drag`, no auto-exploration (v030-09 is «Auto-exploration»'s), no
  error capture (v030-10's).
- The UI graph, the snapshot, the stable-id grammar and the `actions` verb keep their shapes; this chunk reads them.

- The Cold-agent bar's verb count is «Cold-agent bar»'s call (its CARRY names `graph` and `actions`); a new verb this
  chunk adds is named to that entry, not counted here.

- [inferred] «Exercised» has no reader today: the graph's `confirmed` flag reads a registered state's write
  (`signal_registry`), and `SignalRegistry::dispatches()` records the events the bridge dispatched only where an app
  registered a state. A handler-coverage count needs a record of which (element, event) handlers a run reached that
  holds on every app, registry or not — to be read in `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/{dioxus_document,signal_registry,graph}.rs`.

- [inferred] The unexercised set is the graph's handlers on the screens the checks reached, not only the last screen: a
  handler on a screen no check showed is unexercised too only if the command can see it. Which screens the count spans
  (the final screen, every screen read during the replays, or the app's whole handler set) is to be settled at P3/P4.

- [inferred] How a set of checks reaches the command is open: replayed in process through `Check::replay` and then read,
  or a verb that names checks (a call naming a path on disk would be a new input class onto every carrier). The choice
  is a P4 fork; any new verb, argument kind, result field or carrier content is a boundary widening, the founder's
  (the playbook's `escalate` patterns are read at P4).

- [inferred] A kept `actions` step's replay holds today by construction (`Check::replay` runs every instance-verb step
  through `Session::run`; `recording_tests` keeps the answer whole) — unmeasured, the claim the owed test measures.

- [inferred] Surfaces a new driver verb would move: `packages/escher-driver/src/{schema,command,execute,describe,json,
  recording,replay,mcp}.rs` and `mcp/listing.rs`, the CLI's verb set, `VERBS` fourteen → fifteen with the pins that hold
  that count (`.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py`, `docs/capabilities.md`, README's tool count,
  `schema_tests.rs`, `cli_tests.rs`, `stand_mcp_tools`), and the cold-agent pipe's verb list is «Cold-agent bar»'s.
- The operator's directive at this take-up: `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-08T20-10-44-phase/relay-1.md` (to be snapped).
- The founder's checklist (2026-10-29), «Handler coverage (v030-07)» row: `~/dev/projects/additional/escher-overseer/relays/adapt-0.3.0-canvas-founder-2026-10-29.md` (to be snapped).
- The overseer's reconnaissance, item 4: `escher-0.4.0-incubator/adapt-0.3.0-for-canvas.md` (gitignored; to be snapped).

- The CARRY's own source: `escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here/inputs/I6-relay-1.md.txt` (that chunk's
  I6, cited by its path, not this chunk's input).

- `8d6c57130342` (HEAD, the last wrap's flip): green · checks 17/17 · wall 1352 s · CI#42504115722 push completed/success.
  Nothing to fold.

title: I3-adapt-0.3.0-for-canvas.md.txt
body:
# Adapting 0.3.0's planned work to the 0.4.0 canvas plans (the escher overseer's reconnaissance, 2026-10-29)

**Why.** The founder, 2026-10-29: «давай теперь сделай разведку чтоб понять возможно то что мы планируем делать сейчас
стоит адаптировать с учетом планов, чтоб не получилось что мы что то строим а в итоге прийдется полностью переделывать
изза новых требований». The 0.4.0 plans are in `canvas-and-node-graph.md`: virtual nodes inside a canvas, the canvas
observed as data, a `drag` verb, and pan and zoom through a transform.

**Read at `a6c6a37c7`**: `escher-0.3.0/requirements.md`, `working-route.md`,
`packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/element_id.rs`, `snapshot.rs`, and `packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs`,
`command.rs`, `wire.rs`. These are the overseer's reading of the code, not measurements.

## What already fits (no rework expected)
- **The snapshot is built from the accesskit tree** (`snapshot.rs:98`: «its id and role from that tree»). That tree
  carries non-DOM nodes natively, so a canvas's virtual nodes can enter it without a new carrier.
- **An action lands on a point.** `click` and `type` press the centre of the target's bounds
  (`execute.rs:360`, `:427-439`). A virtual node with bounds can be clicked the same way, as long as the canvas app
  hit-tests its own pointer events.
- **The wire is versioned** (`wire.rs:37`, `v3`), so a new verb is an additive, versioned change.

## Where 0.3.0 could build something 0.4.0 would have to redo
1. **The stable-id grammar** (`element_id.rs`). Today an id is an author key, an anchored path (`//`), a component path,
   or a document path (`/…`), all derived from DOM and vdom elements. A virtual node has no DOM element. If D2, B3,
   E2's recorded checks and replay store ids in this grammar, 0.4.0 needs a form for `{canvas element}` + `{virtual
   key}` that collides with none of the four. **Adapt in «The UI graph» (v030-05): reserve that form now (a separator no
   current id can hold), even if nothing produces it yet.**
2. **The node model of the UI graph and of «What can I do here»** (v030-05, v030-06). If the graph and the actionable
   list are keyed on a DOM element (`Target.node: NodeId`, `execute.rs:354`), a virtual node does not fit. **Adapt: key
   them on the agent-visible node (the accesskit node with its bounds), with an optional owner element, and let a
   handler sit on an owner element and serve sub-targets.** A canvas typically has one listener that dispatches inside.
3. **Verbs as a closed list in B3 and E2** (v030-06, v030-09). If «What can I do here» and auto-exploration hard-code
   `click`/`type`/`press`/`scroll`, adding `drag` (two points or a node plus a destination) means reshaping both.
   **Adapt: read the per-node verbs from the schema's verb table, and let the recorded-check step format carry verbs
   with more than one target, versioned.**
4. **Handler coverage** (v030-07) counts DOM listeners. A canvas's internal handlers are invisible to it. **Adapt:
   state that limit in its acceptance, so 0.4.0 extends it rather than redefines it.**
5. **Layout explained** (v030-11) reads Taffy and Stylo. A virtual node's place is the app's own. **Adapt: let its
   answer name the "placed by the app inside canvas X" case, so the field set is not closed.**
6. **Bundled fonts** (v030-14). Canvas text (`GlyphRun`) must draw from the same bundled fonts, or a canvas reads
   differently across hosts. **Adapt: in its acceptance, name canvas text as a reader of the bundled set.**
7. **Engine debts** (v030-04). The transform `visible_region` fix should be proven on a pan/zoom container like the
   node graph's (`canvas-and-node-graph.md`).

## What 0.3.0 should not take on
The canvas renderer itself, the CPU renderer's custom-paint gap, `drag`, and virtual-node production all stay in 0.4.0.
The adaptations above keep 0.3.0's shapes open; they add no 0.4.0 capability.

after every replayed step (`inputs#I4`, Q2, the overseer's call), and answers one JSON line. The line names every
handler, as a graph node id with its optional owner and an event name, that appeared on a screen and that no
replayed dispatch reached. No verb is added: `VERBS` stays at fourteen, and the socket, MCP and the cold-agent pipe
are unchanged.

"Exercised" gets a record that holds on every app. Today the graph's only notion of a reached handler is "a dispatch
of its event passed through its element" (`graph.rs:190-195`). That rule reads the `SignalRegistry`'s dispatches,
which exist only where an app registered a state. The stand's load page registers none (research, Mechanism claims).
The new record is a root context the document provides when asked, written on the bridge's `handle_event` path. The
handler's stable id is resolved when the dispatch happens, so a handler whose element its own step removes still
counts (architecture/established-decisions fct-nl4nv5ny). It holds no `NodeId`, logs nothing, and is off unless the
coverage reader turns it on.

The count covers DOM listeners on agent-visible nodes, so a canvas's internal handlers are not counted; 0.4.0 extends
the count rather than redefining it (`inputs#I2`, `inputs#I3`). The chunk also writes the replay test that v030-06
owes (CARRY `cry-sxrivdk3`, `inputs#I1`): a session recorded with an `actions` step, kept, read back, and replayed on
a fresh session of the same app. v030-06 reads verified only once that test passes (per test-plan §5, fct-kzdrls5d).

body:
- **matrix#v030-07** — after a set of kept checks has run on the stand, one command lists exactly the handlers none
  of them exercised.
  - The command is `escher-session coverage <app> <check>…`, with `escher_driver::handler_coverage` under it.
  - On each of the six served tasks, in both layout modes:
    - a check of one `snapshot` lists exactly `HANDLERS_AT_BOOT`, equal to the graph's handlers on a fresh boot;
    - a check of the task's `GRAPH_DRIVES` lists exactly its `UNEXERCISED_AFTER_DRIVES` row.
  - Two checks list only what neither exercised.
  - The record holds on the load page, which registers no state.
  - A step refused `disabled` exercises nothing, and a keyboard activation exercises the click it dispatches.
  - A handler whose element its own step removes reads exercised.
  - Handlers inside a canvas are not counted: the count reads the UI graph's DOM listeners, and 0.4.0 extends it
    (`inputs#I2`, `inputs#I3`).
  - Witnesses: `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_handler_coverage`, and through the binary
    `cargo test -p seven_guis --locked --test cli_commands`.

- **matrix#v030-06** — its acceptance stands as held. One clause is added: a kept `actions` step replays.
  - A Counter session recorded through `Session::recording_into` with two `actions` steps, read by
    `Check::from_bytes`, holds when replayed through `Check::replay` on a fresh session, all 4 steps run.
  - A copy whose last kept `actions` answer is changed stops the replay at step 3, naming `nodes`.
  - Both hold in both layout modes (`cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_replay`). This is the CARRY
    `cry-sxrivdk3` test, and v030-06 reads verified only on its pass (`inputs#I1`).

- **(security)** The coverage answer holds graph node ids, owner ids, handler event names and two counts only: no
  `NodeId`, control value or typed text, and a typed sentinel occurs 0 times. A named file that is not a check, is
  past the bound, or names another app is refused `malformed`, status 1, holding no byte of its path or contents
  (per security-plan §Input Validation, CLI arguments; security-plan fct-khxrpkj3).

- **(obs)** The two new modules and the new check hold no log site, print, env read or subscriber (entry 9).
  escher-driver keeps 2 `info_span!` (entry 10). `host_log` reads 0 id, name and coverage needles at `trace` under
  both builds (per obs-plan §6 and §8).

- **(arch)** No verb is added and `VERBS` stays at fourteen. `mutation_writer.rs`, `graph.rs`, `signal_registry.rs`,
  every manifest and the committed checks are byte-identical to the base (entry 8). The record takes no document
  borrow across `render_immediate`, and `dioxus_runtime_probe`'s buffered-render pins stay green (entry 6) (per
  architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge).

- **(design)** The role answers one uncoloured line of JSON on stdout under the four exit statuses, adding none (per
  design-system §Surface: cli, cli-output).

- **(tests)** `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run stand` reads failed 0. `ci-leg.sh fast` and `ci-leg.sh doc` pass. CI
  reads green at HEAD with the coverage floors held (entry 19) (per test-plan §10).
- **(a11y)** The `a11y` leg stays green in CI with its fourteen files unchanged (per a11y-plan §9).

- Research files inspected: `graph.rs`, `signal_registry.rs`, `dioxus_document.rs`, `element_id.rs`, `replay.rs`,
  `recording_tests.rs`, `stand_replay.rs`, `tasks/mod.rs`, `stand.rs`, `app.rs`, `cells.rs`, `common/mod.rs`,
  `cli.rs`, `session_host.rs` (research §Files inspected).

- External inputs: `inputs#I1` (the operator's directive), `inputs#I2` (the founder's checklist row), `inputs#I3`
  (the overseer's reconnaissance item 4), `inputs#I4` (the P4 dialog: Q1 the founder's word, Q2 the overseer's call).

- Leaned, per artifact:
  - `mounted` is left out of the count, per the one actionable rule (architecture/standard-contracts fct-ljxizw75).
  - The id is resolved at dispatch (architecture/established-decisions fct-nl4nv5ny binding).
  - A refused step reaches no handler (a11y-plan fct-2hrkecxm).
  - The record is witnessed on an app with no registry (architecture/conventions fct-m3flvoi7).

- A fifteenth instance verb: rejected by the founder's Q1 (`inputs#I4`). A verb also moves every count pin and the
  cold-agent pipe, which belongs to «Cold-agent bar».

- Reading the registry's dispatches as "exercised": the record does not hold on an app with no registered state,
  such as the load page (research, Mechanism claims).

- Resolving reached `NodeId`s after the step: this misses a handler whose element its own step removes (Cells'
  `cell-input` left by Enter). A dropped node's id stops resolving (architecture/design-philosophy fct-rxrxih7j).
- A field on `DioxusState`: it lives in `mutation_writer.rs`, which stays byte-equal to upstream.

- Reading the `data-dioxus-id` mark or listener attributes: they over-report removed listeners
  (a11y-plan/screen-reader-support fct-cbzuzrms).

- A record always on: it would put a whole element walk on every dispatch of every Dioxus document. It is off by
  default and switched on by the coverage reader alone.
- Changing the graph's shape or its `ran` rule: the graph, `unconfirmed` and `stand_graph` stay as they are.
- Committing a new kept check: the two Counter checks stay the one exception (security S1, obs S5).
- A check path on any carrier but the role's own argv (a tool call, a socket call, an MCP argument): not ratified.

- The role reads the caller's own files named on argv. This is a new input class onto the command line, the founder's
  ratified widening (`inputs#I4`).

- Bubbling: a dispatch's chain holds the target and its ancestors, so an ancestor's listener of the same event reads
  reached, as the graph's `ran` rule reads it (`graph.rs:190-195`). A `stopPropagation` is unread, a stated limit.

- `handle_event` returns early when no handler of the event's kind exists (`dioxus_document.rs:371-375`), so such a
  dispatch records nothing. That is correct, since no handler is on it.

- The stand registers every task's state (`git grep -n -c use_graph_signal -- examples/seven_guis/src`), so the
  registry-less witness is the load page (`stand.rs:186-199`) and step 2's unit page.

- Expected amendments (wrap):
  - architecture §Standard Contracts → Driver session: the `coverage` role, `handler_coverage`, `Coverage`,
    `HandlerRef`, re-export count.
  - architecture §Standard Contracts → Dioxus DOM bridge: `ReachedHandler`, `record_reached`, `reached_handlers`, the
    record on `handle_event`'s path.
  - architecture §Established Decisions → Driver session: check files named on the role's argv, a ratified boundary
    widening. Pattern `rul-izni57qv`; answered by the founder's own word, relayed by the overseer (`inputs#I4`, Q1),
    so the wrap halts on it once as the answer card.
  - security-plan §Input Validation, CLI arguments: the role, its bounded read and its `malformed` refusal holding
    nothing of the path; the same pattern and answer.
  - security-plan §Threat Model Summary: a kept check named on the command line, an untrusted input read by
    `Check::from_bytes`.
  - obs-plan §6 Log Coverage: no site added by the role, the reader or the record; `host_log`'s coverage run.
  - test-plan §3, §5, §10: `stand_handler_coverage`; the owed `actions` replay discharged (amd-i4iccah5); the stand
    and reader counts.
  - design-system §Surface: cli: a cli-coverage item.
  - layout-templates §Surface: cli: the role's four endings and usage line.
  - The screens-spanned decision (`inputs#I4`, Q2) is the overseer's call as delegate. Its line rides
    test-plan §5 PROVISIONAL, discharged at the epoch boundary (`rul-3ndrhilc`).

# The founder's word: adapt 0.3.0's open entries to the 0.4.0 canvas plans (2026-10-29)

**His words, typed in the escher overseer session on 2026-10-29:**
- The ask: «давай теперь сделай разведку чтоб понять возможно то что мы планируем делать сейчас стоит адаптировать с
  учетом планов, чтоб не получилось что мы что то строим а в итоге прийдется полностью переделывать изза новых
  требований».
- On the overseer's proposal (no route change; each adaptation goes into its entry's phase inputs): «Ок но надо тогда
  записать это чтоб в процессе не потерять».

**The source:** `~/dev/projects/escher/escher-0.4.0-incubator/adapt-0.3.0-for-canvas.md` (the reconnaissance) and
`canvas-and-node-graph.md` (the 0.4.0 plans: canvas layers «1 3», the canvas observed as data, `drag`, the node graph).

## The checklist, one row per 0.3.0 entry. At each `/andromeda-phase`, snap THIS file and the source into its inputs.

| Entry (working-route) | Adaptation it carries | Done |
|---|---|---|
| Engine debts (v030-04) | Prove the `visible_region`-under-transform fix on a pan/zoom container like the node graph's | ☑ snapped 2026-10-31 (I3, I4); the fixture is written under every option of F1 |
| The UI graph (v030-05) | Reserve a virtual-node id form (`{canvas element}` + `{virtual key}`), one that collides with none of today's four. Key the graph on the agent-visible node (accesskit node + bounds) with an optional owner element. A handler may sit on an owner and serve sub-targets | ☑ snapped 2026-11-07 (the phase's take-up, inputs); his fork 2 reserved `{owner}///{key}` |
| What can I do here (v030-06) | Same node model. The per-node verbs come from the schema's verb table, with no closed list | ☑ snapped 2026-11-08 (the phase's take-up); P4 Q2 reads the verbs from VERBS through the executor's own check, Q4 the graph's node rule |
| Handler coverage (v030-07) | State in its acceptance that handlers inside a canvas are not counted. 0.4.0 extends it | ☑ snapped 2026-11-08 (inputs I2, I3); the plan's v030-07 acceptance and its limits state it, a deferral to 0.4.0 on the P5 card |
| Auto-exploration (v030-09) | The verbs come from B3 and the schema. The recorded-check step format can carry a verb with two targets, versioned | ☐ |
| Layout explained (v030-11) | The answer can name «placed by the app inside canvas X». The field set is not closed | ☐ |
| Bundled fonts (v030-14) | Canvas text (`GlyphRun`) reads the same bundled set | ☐ |

Each is a direction for the phase, not a decision. Where an adaptation changes a contract or widens a boundary, the
phase brings it to the founder as a fork. None of them adds a 0.4.0 capability to 0.3.0.

      context at `ScopeId::ROOT` through `runtime.provide_context`; a second call keeps the one record.
    - `DioxusDocument::reached_handlers(&self) -> Vec<ReachedHandler>` — `reached.rs:97-105`. The handlers in
      first-reached order, deduplicated by (id, event); empty when the record was never switched on.

      `runtime.has_context::<ReachedRecord>(ScopeId::ROOT)` holds, the record is written after the event-kind and
      dioxus-id early returns and before `runtime.handle_event`. For each node of `chain` whose current listeners
      hold `event.name()`, it inserts that node's stable id with the event name. The id is resolved there, so a
      handler whose own run removes its element still counts. The `DocGuard` is a temporary dropped before
      `runtime.handle_event`, and `poll`, `initial_build` and `flush_queued_mounted_events` are untouched. The
      `SignalRegistry` arm is unchanged beside it, and every other document pays one `has_context` lookup per
      dispatch.

      - Accepted: the coverage line on stdout, status 0. A boot that fails: the session error, status 3.

## 2026-11-08-handler-coverage — the escher-session coverage role's answer line, endings and refusals
**Section:** Self-Validation Protocol (body: the subjects list); Surface: cli › Component Patterns (surface: the new `values · cli-coverage` group)
**Change:**
- The subjects list gains `cli-coverage` after `cli-actions`.
- New group `values · cli-coverage`, its first item: `escher-session coverage <app> <check>...` replays each named kept check of `<app>` on a fresh session and answers one uncoloured line of JSON `{"unexercised":[{"id":…,"owner":…,"event":…}],"checks":n,"held":m}` on stdout, status `0` — the UI graph's handlers, read at boot and after each replayed step, that no given check exercised, `owner` left out when absent; its endings are the command line's four (`0` accepted · `1` refused `malformed` · `2` usage · `3` session error), none added; the line carries ids, owner ids, event names and two counts only.
- Its second item: the role's one shape is `coverage <app> <check>...` — an app the binary boots, then one or more check paths, no `--session` and no `--record` word among them — and any other shape is a usage ending, status `2`; each path is read bounded at 1,048,576 + 1 bytes and parsed strictly, and a file that cannot be read, one past the bound, one that is no check and a check of another app are each refused `malformed`, status `1`, the refusal holding nothing of the path or the file.
**Why:** the report's Symbols / APIs (the role, its reader, its answer line and endings) and its Outcome (design) MET, one uncoloured JSON line with none of the four exit statuses added, and (security) MET on the refusals. The role's crossing — kept-check files named on argv — is a boundary widening ratified by the founder's own word at P4 Q1, relayed verbatim by the overseer (inputs#I4); its records here were confirmed at this wrap's answer card Q1 by the overseer as delegate, PROVISIONAL (`delegate overseer`), to be superseded by the founder's own word in his batch at the epoch boundary.
**Kept:** the `escher-session` item stands as written — one line of JSON per command and the four exit statuses; the coverage role adds no exit status.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-08T22-56-33-wrap/

the other five carry none and still take `advance`, which moves their session's clock alone (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18)). `start <task> [--record <dir>]` checks its recording directory itself before it spawns, then spawns the same binary in its host role, `serve <task> --session <dir> [--record <dir>]` (passing `--record` to the host); since 2026-10-19-session-recording `--record <dir>`, taken at most once on `start`, the host role and the `mcp` role, keeps the session as one owner-only replayable check — `check-{n}.json` (`0600`, never replacing a file) in a `0700` directory whose parent must exist, never removed by escher, holding per call its verb, arguments, acceptance, the answer's digest and, since 2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay, the answer itself as an `answer` key — the line the driver wrote, masked as on every carrier, a shot's kept as `{"width":…,"height":…}` without its `png` — read back and replayed by `Check::replay` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-19: F1 A · F2 B, F3 B) — a directory open to its group or others refused as the session error `record-dir-not-private` (exit 3, `start` spawning nothing), a recording that ends answering `recording-failed` (exit 3; over MCP `isError`); the host serves until `stop` or its 30-minute idle expiry and writes nothing to stdout; every other command is one client run that answers one line of JSON on stdout (exit `0` accepted · `1` refused · `2` usage · `3` session error — the four read from `EXIT_STATUSES` and served by `help`), save `help` (since 2026-10-12-self-description), which needs no `--session` — it admits at most one and reads it not — and answers the tool's self-description with status `0`, reaching no session; the `mcp` role lists it as its fourteenth tool, last, `graph` after `lint` and `actions` after `graph`. Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot the seventh instance verb, `screenshot [--id <id>] --session <dir>`, answers one uncoloured line `{"width":…,"height":…,"png":"<base64>"}` on stdout, exit 0 — the whole screen, or with `--id` the element cropped to the part of its bounds that can be seen — an app with no font it can paint text with refused `fonts-unavailable` and an element shot that crops to no pixel `off-screen`, exit 1; over the `mcp` role an accepted shot is an `image` block (`image/png`, base64) then a text block, the line without `png`. The eighth instance verb, `lint --session <dir>`, takes no argument (one named refused `malformed`) and answers one uncoloured line `{"findings":[…]}` on stdout, exit 0, each finding keyed `id` · `defect` · `bounds` then its reason's keys — ids, closed words and numbers only — an app with no font it can paint text with refused `fonts-unavailable`, exit 1, a `lint` step kept under `--record` like every instance verb; over the `mcp` role an accepted `lint` answers its JSON line of findings as one text block. The ninth instance verb, `graph --session <dir>`, after `lint`, takes no argument (one named refused `malformed`) and answers one uncoloured line `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…]}` on stdout, exit 0, carrying ids, component names, handler event names, registered state names, closed flag words and booleans only, never a value; over the `mcp` role an accepted `graph` answers its JSON line `{"nodes","states"}` as one text block. The tenth instance verb, `actions --session <dir>`, after `graph`, takes no argument (one named refused `malformed`) and answers one uncoloured line `{"nodes":[{"id":…,"owner":…,"keyed":…,"verbs":[{"verb":…,"cause":…}]}]}` on stdout, exit 0, `owner` and `cause` left out when absent, carrying ids, owner ids, the table's verb words, closed cause words and booleans only, never a value, typed text or `NodeId`, the answer unpaged; over the `mcp` role an accepted `actions` answers its JSON line `{"nodes"}` as one text block. The first instance verb, `snapshot [--part <part>] --session <dir>`, takes an optional `--part` (a whole number, 1 to 1000) and answers one uncoloured line on stdout, exit 0 — `{"text":…}` for a whole screen, `{"text":…,"part":n,"parts":m}` for a screen read in parts, from part 1 without `--part`, a part past the last the empty text with the same `parts`, a `--part` outside its bound refused `malformed`, exit 1; over the `mcp` role a paged `snapshot` answers its JSON line `{"text","part","parts"}` as one text block, a whole screen still the bare screen text. The former two-argument form `<task> <state-dir>` is gone. A fourth role, `escher-session coverage <app> <check>...` — one app the binary boots, then one or more kept-check paths, no `--session` and no `--record` word among them, any other shape usage (stderr, exit 2) — reads each path bounded at `MAX_CHECK_BYTES + 1` and parses it by `Check::from_bytes` (unreadable, past the bound, no check or a check of another app refused `malformed`, exit 1), replays each check on a fresh boot through the same boot `main` hands to the command line and answers one uncoloured line `{"unexercised":[{"id":…,"owner":…,"event":…}],"checks":n,"held":m}` on stdout, exit 0, `owner` left out when absent; a boot that fails ends with the session error, exit 3. Since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface its `mcp` role, `escher-session mcp [--record <dir>]` (the `--record` since 2026-10-19-session-recording), is an MCP server over its standard streams (`escher_driver::serve_mcp`): its `start` tool, its `enum` naming the six, boots one of the six served tasks through the same boot and holds it in process, adding no markup; it writes protocol lines only on stdout and ends with nothing there. record.title: Handler coverage
record.requirement: One command lists the handlers no recorded check exercised, read from the UI graph
record.observed_gap: Nothing says which handlers no check reached.

verification.acceptance: After a set of kept checks has run on the stand, one command lists exactly the handlers none of them exercised: the command-line role `escher-session coverage <app> <check>…`, over `escher_driver::handler_coverage`, replays each named kept check on a fresh session of the app, reads the UI graph at boot and after every replayed step, and answers one JSON line of the (id, owner, event) handlers no replayed dispatch reached, `mounted` excluded. On the six served tasks in both layout modes, a check of one `snapshot` lists exactly the boot screen's handlers (`HANDLERS_AT_BOOT`, equal to the graph's handlers on a fresh boot), and a check of each task's `GRAPH_DRIVES` lists exactly its `UNEXERCISED_AFTER_DRIVES` row; two checks list only what neither exercised; the reached record holds on the load page, which registers no state; a step refused `disabled` exercises nothing and a keyboard activation exercises the click it dispatches; a handler whose element its own step removes reads exercised. Handlers inside a canvas are not counted: the count reads the UI graph's DOM listeners, and 0.4.0 extends it (`cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked --test stand_handler_coverage`; through the binary `cargo test -p seven_guis --locked --test cli_commands`).
